purpose: Before a paid campaign, check that one Modal H100 can serve the harness's pinned model with its publisher's vLLM command on the pinned vLLM image.

model.chosen_by: poc_modal.py choose-model on 2026-11-21: most downloaded FP8 checkpoint from Qwen, Z.ai and DeepSeek (6,506,958 downloads) that fits one H100 and has a published one-H100 vLLM command without speculative decoding

attempts.cause: ValueError: max_num_seqs (1024) exceeds available Mamba cache blocks (818). Each decode sequence requires one Mamba cache block, so CUDA graph capture cannot proceed. Please lower max_num_seqs to at most 818 or increase gpu_memory_utilization.
RuntimeError: Process RustFrontend (PID: 76) died with exit code 1

conclusion: The publisher's one-H100 command does not start on vLLM 0.22.1: 48 of the model's 64 layers keep a recurrent state, one cache block per running request; vLLM found 818 such blocks and refused its default of 1,024 requests at once. vLLM's defaults alone (InferCrane's generic vLLM starting setup) fail the same way.

With --max-num-seqs 512 the engine starts, but the Rust HTTP frontend the publisher's environment selects exits; with vLLM's Python frontend the server serves, refuses a request without its key, answers, calls a tool, and exports every engine metric family the control plane scrapes.
The harness's current setup is therefore the publisher's command plus --max-num-seqs 512, on the Python frontend. A campaign runs 32 requests at once, so the cap changes nothing it measures.
